_readme: Every machine-checkable fact the plugin asserts, with the source it was verified against and the date it was verified.
Tier 0 asserts that Section 0 of the agent definition agrees with this file.
Tier 2 (weekly) asserts that this file still agrees with live upstream sources.
When you correct a fact: change it here, cite the source in the commit body, and set a fresh verifiedOn.

release.cadence: mainline monthly, on the Tuesday before the third Wednesday; next line weekly on Tuesdays
release.deprecationPolicy: a deprecation ships in at least one mainline release before removal
release.verifiedBy: fetched manifest; releaseVersion field read directly

node.verifiedBy: npm pack of the published tarball; field read from the template, not from documentation

createApp.source: npm:@backstage/create-app@0.9.0 dist/index.cjs.js (commander option list) and templates/default-app/package.json.hbs
createApp.verifiedBy: npm pack; option list read from the shipped commander program, script list read from the shipped template

frontendSystem.verifiedBy: read the shipped template files: App.tsx imports @backstage/frontend-defaults; index.tsx calls App.createRoot()

communityPlugins.verifiedBy: registry HEAD on sampled @backstage-community/plugin-* names extracted from the plugin content

supplyChain._note: Traps that a copy-pasted command would walk into. Enforced by Tier 1.

squattedBareNames.name: backstage-cli
squattedBareNames.risk: `npx backstage-cli <cmd>` installs an unrelated third-party package published by a different maintainer, not the Backstage CLI.
squattedBareNames.verifiedBy: https://registry.npmjs.org/backstage-cli returns 200 for an unrelated package: 'The CLI companion that lets you upload builds to your Backstage Server.'

supportMatrix._note: See OPEN-DECISIONS.md #4. oldestSupportedLine is the oldest line the skills' guidance was WRITTEN against, not a line anything has been tested on.

stalenessBudget._note: Tier 2 policy. A 'line' is one mainline minor (1.53 -> 1.54).
stalenessBudget.rationale: One line behind is normal — Backstage ships monthly and the baseline is re-verified on a weekly job. Two is a missed cycle worth an issue. Three means the plugin has been asserting facts about a release line nobody has looked at in a quarter, which is where a removed API becomes an instruction the agent acts on.

linkChecking._note: Hosts that rate-limit aggressively enough to make link checking flaky. Excluded from the every-commit tier, still checked weekly.

documentation._note: Verified URL shapes. backstage.io has no release-notes index page — only per-line pages. Tier 2 re-checks both.
documentation.verifiedBy: fetched the sitemap and probed /docs/releases/ directly; it returns 404
